    StartersVenice cicchetti, three toppings on toastBaguette toasts with smoked cod cream, prosciutto and fig, or artichoke and parsleyHow to make it1 baguette, sliced3 tbsp olive oil200g smoked cod1 garlic clove100g prosciutto4 fresh figs, sliced1 jar artichoke hearts, sliced2 tbsp chopped parsleyToast the baguette slices with a little olive oil.Poach the cod until flaking, then whip with olive oil and garlic until creamy.Spread a third of the toasts with the cod.Top a third with prosciutto and fig, and the rest with artichoke and parsley.Netherlands tulip field friesThick twice-fried fries in paper cones with a big spoon of mayonnaiseHow to make it1kg potatoes1 L vegetable oil for frying2 tsp sea salt flakes150g mayonnaiseCut the potatoes into thick fries, rinse and dry well.Fry in the oil at 140°C until soft, then rest.Fry again at 190°C until crisp.Toss with sea salt and serve in paper cones with mayonnaise on top.Prague trdelník with cinnamon walnut sugarThe night at the festival in PragueHow to make itAs written, serves 4Sweet yeast dough spiralled round foil-wrapped rolling pins, baked golden and rolled in cinnamon sugar and crushed walnuts, warm and chewy.Mix 300g plain flour, 7g dried yeast, 40g sugar, 1 egg, 40g soft butter and 150ml warm milk into a soft dough, knead 5 minutes and prove 1 hour.Wrap 2 rolling pins in buttered foil.Roll the dough into long 1cm ropes and coil tightly around the pins.Brush with melted butter, roll in 100g sugar mixed with 2 tsp cinnamon and 50g crushed walnuts, and bake at 200°C for 15 minutes.Slide off and cut into rings.Fritto misto with lemonFury's waiting. Peter's ghosting him again.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsWater elemental seafood spaghettiSpaghetti with prawns, mussels and clams in garlic, white wine and chilliHow to make it5 garlic cloves, crushed1/4 tsp chilli flakes3 tbsp olive oil250ml white wine300g green prawns500g mussels, scrubbed500g clams, purged500g cooked spaghetti3 tbsp chopped parsleyCook 225g dried spaghetti in well salted water until just tender, then drain.Cook the spaghetti.Soften the garlic and chilli in the olive oil.Add the wine, prawns, mussels and clams, cover and cook until the shells open, discarding any that stay shut.Toss through the spaghetti and parsley.Tower Bridge flathead and chipsThe final fight at Tower BridgeHow to make itAs written, serves 4Flathead fillets in a crisp lager batter fried golden, with thick double-cooked chips, minted mushy peas and tartare sauce.Cut 1kg potatoes into thick chips and fry at 140°C for 6 minutes, then drain.Whisk 200g self-raising flour with 300ml cold lager and salt.Dust 600g flathead fillets in flour, dip in the batter and fry at 180°C for 4 minutes until crisp.Fry the chips again at 190°C for 3 minutes.Simmer 400g frozen peas for 4 minutes, mash with butter and mint.Serve with tartare and lemon.SweetsE.D.I.T.H. tiramisuCoffee-dipped ladyfingers layered with mascarpone cream, dusted with cocoaHow to make it3 egg yolks80g caster sugar250g mascarpone200ml cream, whipped200g savoiardi biscuits300ml strong coffee, cooled2 tbsp cocoaWhisk the yolks with the sugar until pale, then fold in the mascarpone and whipped cream.Dip the savoiardi briefly in the coffee and layer with the cream in a dish. Repeat.Chill overnight.Dust with cocoa to serve.DrinksNed and Betty's peach bellini mocktailPeach puree topped with sparkling apple juice, no alcoholHow to make it4 ripe peaches, peeled and stoned1 tbsp caster sugar1 tsp lemon juice600ml sparkling apple juiceBlend the peaches with the sugar and lemon until smooth.Spoon a few spoons of puree into each glass.Slowly top with chilled sparkling apple juice and stir gently.Blood orange Italian sodaNight Monkey's order.
